conviction_note: The event is confirmed by the company's own date release (Oct 6, before the open). Every company-level fact I found is already public: Q2 was guided 'slightly lower sales, lower adj EPS YoY', the FY27 $2.70-3.25 range was reiterated, the Kalwall and GroGlass deals were announced, and the board additions and the ABI slump are on record. So the 19% slide from about $43.5 (early Aug) to $35.37 has no cause I could document, and an unexplained drawdown is worth 0; honest zero.
bar: Q2 FY27 adjusted EPS $0.63. Two estimate sources agree: Zacks/MarketBeat via Defense World, https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/09/29/apogee-enterprises-apog-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday.html, and Finviz 'EPS next Q' $0.63, https://finviz.com/stock?t=APOG. Revenue consensus is about $359.5M (MarketBeat only). The company guide is directional only: Q2 sales slightly below $358.2M and adj EPS below $0.98 (Q2 FY26), per the Q1 FY27 call, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/26/apogee-apog-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/. FY27 adj EPS guide is $2.70-3.25, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000058/a53026fy27q1results.htm, against FY consensus of about $2.82-2.94. The +5% print_vs_bar rests only on the habit of beating ($0.57 vs $0.43 in Q1 FY27, $0.98 vs $0.86 in Q2 FY26). It is not a finding.
positioning_check: Finviz (as of 2026-09-30 close): short float 4.63%, short ratio 4.33 days, https://finviz.com/stock?t=APOG. Not crowded. There is no usable option chain (zero open interest, ATM legs not two-sided), so there is no skew and no implied move. The baseline anchors on the median historical reaction of 12.72%. The 20-day run-up is -5.91%, the stock is 27.7% off its 52-week high and the Finviz quarter performance is -19.3%.

outside_window.finding: PMC Property Group v. Apogee Wausau Group / Viracon (E.D. Pa. 2:24-cv-02945), over nickel-sulfide glass breakage at three Philadelphia towers. In late August 2026 the court dismissed the parent and some claims and let the manufacturing-defect and unjust-enrichment claims go forward. There is no damages figure and no dated catalyst inside the window, so it is not sized.
outside_window.resolves_by: unknown (litigation ongoing; no dated event in window)

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filing list since 2026-06-01 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000006845&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40): the 8-Ks are Kalwall closing (07-01), director appointments (08-05 Hayek and Krishna, 09-14 Streich, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000091/apogpressrelease-jstreic.htm), the GroGlass agreement (09-03, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000087/apog-20260902.htm) and GroGlass closing (09-23). No executive departure, no guidance update, no 2.02 or 8.01 pre-announcement.

Q1 FY27 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000063/apog-20260530.htm): nothing new in contingencies. Term loan $209.4M, revolver $28.0M, buyback authority of 1.53M shares left. The financing is acquisition funding (Kalwall $105M, GroGlass about EUR62.5M) at about 1.3x leverage, which reads as neither distress nor news.

GroGlass economics are disclosed (about $30M revenue, about 25% adj EBITDA margin; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/apogee-apog-agreed-acquire-groglass-024507584.html). It closed 09-18, which is Q3, so it does not land in the reported quarter. Folding it into the guide is mechanical and was disclosed.

IEEPA tariff refund angle: Apogee's tariff exposure is mainly Section 232 aluminum, which is not refundable. The EDGAR full-text search for 'IEEPA' on CIK 6845 returned 0 hits (efts.sec.gov), and the Q1 call has no mention of a refund.

AIA ABI August 2026 at 47.2, up from July's 46.6 and still contracting (https://www.aia.org/resource-center/abi-august-2026-architecture-firm-billings-continue-decline). This does contradict management's assumed H2 'improvement in underlying market conditions'. But it is public macro data that the company has not linked to its own numbers, the trend did not worsen after the guide, and the 19% slide plus an FY consensus below the guide midpoint already reflect it. Not a finding.

Aluminum: LME about $3,180-3,280/t in late September and a Midwest premium around $2,000/t (https://www.packagingdive.com/news/aluminum-steel-tinplate-tariffs-midwest-premium-2026/813711/). Already public, and management put surcharges in place in Q1.

Peer read: Tecnoglass Q2 2026 posted record revenue and a record $1.38B backlog (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tecnoglass-reports-second-quarter-2026-110000962.html). That is a different end market and product, so not transmissible to Apogee's glass business.
Viracon/Apogee WARN notices and layoffs in 2026: none found beyond the Nov 2025 Mesquite TX notice (https://www.usglassmag.com/apogee-architectural-metals-plans-texas-layoffs/).

Price tape from 2026-07-22 to 09-30 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/apog/history/): a steady slide from $43.52 (08-07) to $35.37 on normal volume. The one spike, 647k on 09-18, matches GroGlass closing and quad witching. No documentable cause.
baseline_tension: I found nothing that cuts against the baseline. There is no skew to read, and the slide (-5.9% over 20 days, -19% on the quarter) has no documented cause, so the price already holds everything public. The name's history (median absolute move 12.7%, direction set by the guide) says the print will move it a lot, but nothing I found predicts the sign.
lessons_applied: nothing changed (lesson 5 confirms the ABI macro read and the unexplained drawdown stay at 0; lesson 6 confirms the litigation sits outside the window)
